description: System-owned phase, role, report, and execution contracts used to build BridgePacket fields. Agent prompts may explain role behavior, but these contracts own packet structure.
default_forbidden_actions: destructive filesystem operations outside writable scopes

external network calls through Bash or project code that are unrelated to the accepted packet, require secrets/tokens/payment/manual license acceptance, or expose private data; task-authorized public no-token acquisition and task-relevant research are allowed when the phase/tools permit them

destructive or global dependency/environment changes unless explicitly approved; task-scoped dependency repair, version pinning, cache rebuilds, or local tooling bypasses are allowed in L4 implement/execute when needed and auditable
implementation content edits during L3 artifact curation unless the file is human-facing documentation already in L3 doc scope
physical deletion of user/project artifacts unless the item is clearly regenerable trash, an empty duplicate, or explicitly approved

resolution_policy: actively resolve identities from the frozen instruction and current repository state
if the user did not request a change, inherit the current active dataset/prompt/config basis and say where it came from
for model or method comparisons, name the concrete checkpoints or checkpoint-selection rule for each side
do not let L4 implement or execute infer unresolved identities silently
unknown identity fields must be marked unknown, blocked, or escalated with a concrete reason

required_evidence: runtime event ids
instruction coverage disposition
semantic identity resolution

success_criteria: bridge leader collected a report from the team
every instruction coverage checklist item is completed, deferred with reason, blocked, or escalated

responsibilities: produce upstream interpretation, assumptions, plan critique, peer challenges, and confidence-loop advisory judgment
produce independent upstream advisory judgment, critique chiefmate-a/chiefmate-c, and challenge weak convergence
produce additional GPT-main peer critique, actively rebut weak peer convergence, challenge chiefmate-a/chiefmate-b, and run confidence-loop validation

required_evidence: pseudocode flow for each new major technical plan or explicit not_applicable reason

responsibilities: clarify active logs, datasets, checkpoints, outputs, archive boundaries, and traceability; use Bash only for bounded filesystem curation

on every invocation, compare current docs, active artifacts, manifests, reports, and latest runtime evidence for stale or conflicting project-state claims that could mislead downstream phases; curate in scope or report the exact follow-up
inspect implementation-facing repo/config state and surface required changes before implementation without running commands
refresh CLAUDE.md and bounded human-facing repository documentation when needed

on every invocation, inspect enough current runtime evidence, reports, manifests, and active repo docs to identify documentation drift against accepted project state, semantic identities, artifact status, or next-phase guidance; update in scope or report the legal follow-up

required_evidence: current user intent confirmed refined superseded blocked or escalated with reason

responsibilities: make approved code/config changes and collect implementation-owned dry-run smoke warmup or first-step validation evidence before execute handoff
judge post-implementation readiness, including whether implementation-owned dry-run smoke warmup or first-step evidence is present before execute, and recommend proceed, repair, reroute, or stop

validation_requirements: implementation handoff distinguishes dry-run/debug evidence from formal-run readiness
implementation-owned dry-run, smoke, warmup, or first-step validation evidence checks code path and resource feasibility before execute handoff, or an approved blocker explains why it cannot run
execution entrypoint, configs, data/input manifests, expected outputs, and non-dry-run command are present or explicitly blocked with approved reason

proceed-to-execute handoff contains no self-disqualifying caveat such as proxy/readiness-only, placeholder/scaffold-only, synthetic metrics, or not formal benchmark evidence for the approved deliverable
success_criteria: L4 implement does not claim proceed-to-execute based only on dry run, static check, toy run, placeholder output, or blocker-only manifest
L4 implement treats dry-run smoke warmup and first-step checks as implementation debugging and readiness work, not as execute work or formal deliverables
L4 implement leaves a formal execute handoff with concrete command, cwd, configs, inputs, expected outputs, and blocker evidence, or routes repair before execute

L4 implement must not classify weaker proxy/readiness outputs as ready for a plan that requires real benchmark, model-generation, or formal deliverable evidence unless the packet explicitly approves that weaker boundary

required_evidence: real non-dry-run entrypoint or explicit approved blocker
formal command and cwd or blocker reason
config paths and data/input manifest paths or blocker reason
expected output/checkpoint/log paths
implementation-owned dry-run smoke warmup or first-step validation evidence with command cwd result and memory or resource observation when applicable, or approved blocker reason
dry-run/static evidence labeled as debugging only, not formal completion

responsibilities: run the approved workflow and record exact execution evidence
audit execution artifacts, terminal status, outcome classification, and recommended next route

validation_requirements: generated formal log folders include internal manifests
exit-code success is not acceptable completion unless the formal run has a readable manifest bound to the current run_id, bridge_window_id, task_id, and formal stage
log manifests include required identity command cwd batchbasis gpu memory and semantic fields
formal log manifests record approved target quantity versus observed terminal quantity, or a not_applicable reason for non-countable formal work

before L4 execute treats team idle or teammate completion as finish-ready, current GPU resource-utilization evidence is checked against actual selected-device availability, batch or microbatch basis, and semantics-preserving adaptation options when GPU execution is involved

formal execution preserves approved semantic scope such as dataset coverage, evaluation sample count, generation length, sequence/truncation, prompt/template, metric, model, checkpoint, and method settings unless the packet explicitly approves a weaker boundary
success_criteria: formal execution log folders are not identified by filename alone; each generated log folder has an internal manifest with identity, command, cwd, batchbasis, GPU/memory, and natural-language semantic fields
L4 execute treats missing, stale, unreadable, or nonmatching run/window/task manifests as execute packaging defects even when terminal commands exited 0

L4 execute does not finish solely because a command exited or the team went idle if GPU utilization evidence is materially low and unresolved semantics-preserving resource adaptation remains available inside the packet boundary

L4 execute uses resource adaptation only for semantics-preserving knobs such as GPU, batch, microbatch, accumulation, precision, or memory toggles; it does not call a reduced sample-count, reduced generation-length, missing-family, or other weaker semantic run acceptable unless explicitly approved

required_evidence: log manifest path
formal execution parameter manifest
manifest required fields checklist
formal completion evidence with approved target quantity versus observed terminal quantity or not_applicable reason
batchbasis
gpu_id
current GPU resource-utilization sanity check before finish-ready team idle or completion when GPU execution is involved
observed-vs-available VRAM disposition and resource-adaptation evidence or best-available deviation rationale when utilization is materially low
smoke memory observed when smoke ran
warmup memory observed when warmup ran
natural-language model dataset method semantics

responsibilities: perform complete independent anomaly diagnosis before peer review; reject simple mechanical missing-artifact or incomplete-handoff work back to the owning phase
perform complete independent anomaly diagnosis before peer review; reject simple mechanical missing-artifact or incomplete-handoff work back to the owning phase

perform complete independent anomaly diagnosis before peer review, with extra emphasis on rebutting weak peer causal convergence; reject simple mechanical missing-artifact or incomplete-handoff work back to the owning phase

validation_requirements: anomaly task describes a surprising, contradictory, suspicious, or underexplained result/failure requiring causal diagnosis

simple mechanical gaps such as missing files, absent manifests, missing data, dry-run-only handoffs, incomplete implementation validation, missing commands, or stale pointers are routed to l4_implement or l3_bridge instead of anomaly
success_criteria: L4 anomaly analyzes complex causes and alternatives, not ordinary missing-artifact repair
If the packet is only a mechanical completion gap, L4 anomaly returns a reroute recommendation to the owning phase without pretending deep anomaly analysis was needed
